properties.name: A rule the project follows lives in the graph, not in an agent's memory file
properties.statement:
THE RULE, settled 2026-09-19 into THREE PLACES, cheapest first: ① ENCODE IT — a lesson that can become a gate step, a test or a CI job is automated and written down nowhere. ② THE GRAPH — whatever a person or an agent must read and judge, and anything true on another machine, hung off the node it concerns. ③ MEMORY — only what is true of THIS BOX alone. Memory holds a POINTER to a node, never the content.

Anthony, 2026-09-04, when offered a habit for the agent's memory: 'I prefer to add rules to the graph. If for instance I change development to another machine, I don't think memories are transferable. This is one of the reasons for reflow2.'

WHY, in three parts, all his:

① PORTABILITY. A memory file is machine-local and harness-local. The graph is a committed file that travels with the repository, so it resolves on any machine, for any agent, in any harness — `req:content-reaches-every-seat` states the same property for blob pointers and this extends it to governance. A rule only one seat can see is not a project rule.

② THE GRAPH IS THE PLACE THAT CAN ACT ON IT. A DesignRule can carry `enforced`, owe a detector, raise `unstated_rule_enforcement`, and be VIOLATED by a computation. A memory file can do none of those; it is prose an agent may or may not read. `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` is the case in point — it is enforced, it is in the graph, and it was still broken five times on 2026-09-04 by an agent whose memory held a paraphrase of it. The paraphrase reached nobody; the rule at least owes a check.

③ IT IS WHAT REFLOW2 IS FOR. His words: 'this is one of the reasons for reflow2'. A design brain that keeps its own operating rules somewhere it cannot read is the storyflow failure `dec:what-lives-where` describes — prose you navigate rather than a graph you query — applied to the tool's own conduct.

WHAT THE MEMORY FILE IS STILL FOR: who the user is, how they like to be spoken to, where things are on THIS machine, and pointers into the graph. Those are facts about a seat, not rules of a project, and a seat is exactly what a memory file is scoped to.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether breaking it should stop the build. Nothing enforces where a session writes a lesson, and no detector could read a memory file it cannot see. `enforced` is deliberately left unstated here for the owner to rule on, per `dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking`.

SETTLED 2026-09-19, on the brainstorm Anthony called after a session wrote fifteen traps into a machine-local file while this rule sat in the graph unread (dec:idea-what-belongs-in-the-graph-and-what-belongs-in-an-agents-memory-and-why-the-rule-keeps-losing). His word: "Promote your recommended fix."

WHAT MOVED, and why each.

① THE BOUNDARY IS THREE PLACES, NOT TWO. Graph-versus-memory was a false binary: the best home for most of the traps in question was neither. Two of the fifteen were proved encodable the same day — the design-coherence check moved out of a hand habit into the gate script, and a rule about reading refusals carefully was replaced by a refusal that lists the missing fields itself. A lesson that can be automated is not written down at all; what remains is split by WHO MUST READ IT, which is the portability test this rule already made.

② THE RULE NOW CARRIES `steps`, so it arrives at the moments a lesson is legitimately recorded rather than waiting to be looked up. MEASURED BASIS: of 32 DesignRules on 2026-09-19, 10 carried steps. This one carried none and was left advisory (dec:the-four-2026-09-rules-are-advisory-because-no-detector-can-yet-see-a-violation, 2026-09-07); its sibling from that same ruling — rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed — was given a step after being broken a fourth time and has held since. Same author, same day, same advisory status; the one with a delivery point holds.

⚠️ THE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE ENGINEERED AWAY. Writing to an agent's memory file is not an act reflow2 can see, so no rule delivery reaches the moment of violation. Delivery reaches the moments a lesson is CORRECTLY recorded and makes the graph the default there. The remaining guard is option (d), kept and not yet built: every memory file names the graph node it points at, and a file holding content with no node id is the violation — checkable by a small local script, since the memory directory is outside every tree reflow2 reads.

⭐ AND ONE ARGUMENT WITHDRAWN. The session's own counter-argument — that the graph path costs a constructor plus relations plus an export commit, where a file costs one edit — was overstated and is retracted here. Recording an observation is ONE call that needs nobody's permission, and the export happens anyway at the end of every increment. The cost asymmetry that made this look unwinnable is close to zero.
